extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, and literary professionals interested in submitting or learning about the National Book Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Overview page for the National Book Awards describing the prize's mission, the categories honored, availability of medallions/seals, and links to eligibility, deadlines, and submission guidelines for titles published each year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards currently honor the best Fiction, Nonfiction, Poetry, Translated Literature, and Young People’s Literature, published each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the primary prize categories for which titles are considered; detailed category-specific eligibility and submission rules are available under 'Deadlines & Guidelines.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / selection orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Book Awards were established to celebrate the best writing in America and the National Book Foundation's mission is 'to celebrate the best of American literature, to expand its audience, and to enhance the cultural value of great writing in America.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and promotion are guided by this mission—emphasis on literary excellence and cultural value within American literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility, submissions, and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The site references 'Eligibility, the submissions process, current prizes, guidelines, FAQ.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural and substantive eligibility criteria (publication dates, who may submit, format, deadlines, fees, etc.) are handled in the linked 'Deadlines & Guidelines' material; this page signals their existence but does not enumerate specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medallions and digital/seal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Seals and digital image rights are available for NBA Winner, Finalist, and Longlist titles; medallions are also offered for 5 Under 35 honorees and Distinguished Contribution to American Letters medalists (usable for future or backlist titles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners, finalists, longlisted titles and specific honorees may display official seals; guidance on use and licensing of those digital images is provided by the Foundation (details on the linked medallions page).
